PRESS RELEASE
Risks from AI valuations, fiscal imbalances and geoeconomic tensions weigh on financial stability outlook
18 November 2026
Ambitious earnings expectations for AI firms leave financial markets vulnerable to abrupt adjustments
Fiscal imbalances in major advanced economies could lead to global repricing of sovereign risk
Euro area banks and non-banks exposed to geoeconomic tensions and AI, while strong profitability, capital and liquidity keep banking sector resilient
The outlook for euro area financial stability is being shaped by risks stemming from artificial intelligence (AI) valuations, fiscal imbalances and geoeconomic tensions, according to the November 2026 Financial Stability Review, which is published today by the European Central Bank (ECB).
“Risks to euro area financial stability remain elevated, given persistent geoeconomic uncertainty and growing exposure to AI,” said ECB Vice-President Boris Vujčić. “Banks are well placed to withstand shocks, while vulnerabilities are more pronounced in certain non-banks where risks are growing and macroprudential safeguards are less developed.”
The euro area economy has continued to demonstrate resilience despite an energy shock, trade frictions and extreme weather events. Prolonged energy supply disruptions and persistent trade policy uncertainty could, however, test this resilience. 
Enthusiasm about the transformational potential of AI has driven strong gains in global equity markets, despite some recent volatility. Current valuations rely on ambitious earnings expectations which could yet be challenged by financing concerns or by competition from cheaper AI models. Investment in AI infrastructure is increasingly funded through debt, such that a potential change in sentiment could spread losses from equity markets to bond markets. 
In the euro area, elevated debt levels, growing sovereign borrowing needs and shifts towards more news-sensitive and leveraged investors in euro area sovereign bonds are increasing the risk of abrupt repricing episodes, although markets have continued to function in an orderly manner. Geoeconomic uncertainty, higher energy prices and weak economic growth could further strain public finances, allowing governments less room to respond to shocks.
Banks’ and non-banks’ exposures to AI financing and sovereign bonds leave them exposed to repricing risks. While bank asset quality remains sound, higher energy prices and weaker economic conditions could make it harder for households and firms to repay their debts. Closer links between banks and non-banks could spread and amplify shocks across the financial system.
The euro area banking sector is well positioned to absorb potential shocks, underpinned by strong profits, solid capital buffers and ample liquidity. Preserving bank resilience remains a key macroprudential priority, alongside addressing vulnerabilities related to liquidity and high levels of borrowing among some non-banks. Accelerating progress on the EU’s savings and investments union will also be essential to support economic growth and competitiveness while preserving financial stability.

Item 3.03 - Material Modification to Rights of Security Holders.
On November 15, 2026, each outstanding share of Class B common stock, par value $0.001 per share (the “Class B Common Stock”), of Rivian Automotive, Inc. (the “Company”), automatically converted (the “Conversion”) into one share of the Company’s Class A common stock, par value $0.001 per share (the “Class A Common Stock”), pursuant to the terms of the Company’s Restated Certificate of Incorporation (the “Certificate of Incorporation”). 
The Conversion occurred pursuant to Article Fourth, Section A.3.1.2 of the Certificate of Incorporation, which provides that each outstanding share of Class B Common Stock will automatically convert into one share of Class A Common Stock at 5:00 p.m. New York City time on the five-year anniversary of the closing of the Company’s initial public offering of Class A Common Stock. As of immediately prior to the Conversion, 7,825,000 shares of Class B Common Stock had been issued, representing the entire number of Class B Common Stock authorized under the Certificate of Incorporation, and 3,912,500 shares of Class B Common Stock remained outstanding, reflecting the prior conversion of 3,912,500 shares of Class B Common Stock to Class A Common Stock pursuant to Article Fourth, Section A.3.1 of the Certificate of Incorporation. Immediately following the Conversion, there were approximately 1,459,886,616 shares of Class A Common Stock outstanding.
Article Fourth, Section A.3.1.4 of the Certificate of Incorporation provides that shares of Class B Common Stock that are converted into shares of Class A Common Stock as provided in Article Fourth, Section A.3.1 of the Certificate of Incorporation will be retired and cancelled and may not be reissued. Following the Conversion, on November 16, 2026, the Company filed a Certificate of Retirement (the “Certificate of Retirement”) with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware pursuant to Section 243(b) of the Delaware General Corporation Law (the “DGCL”), which effected the retirement of the 7,825,000 shares of Class B Common Stock that were previously issued but no longer outstanding. Pursuant to Section 243(b) of the DGCL, upon its effectiveness, the Certificate of Retirement had the effect of eliminating from the Certificate of Incorporation all references to the Class B Common Stock.
The Conversion had the following effects, among others, on holders of shares of Class B Common Stock: 
•Voting Power. Prior to the Conversion, holders of shares of Class B Common Stock were entitled to cast ten votes per share on any matter submitted to the stockholders of the Company for a vote or approval. As a result of the Conversion, all former holders of shares of Class B Common Stock are now holders of an equal number of shares of Class A Common Stock, which are entitled to cast only one vote per share on matters submitted to the stockholders. In addition, the provisions of the Certificate of Incorporation and Delaware law that entitled the holders of shares of Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock, in certain circumstances, to separate class voting rights are no longer applicable as a result of the Conversion.
•Economic Interests. Because holders of shares of Class A Common Stock are entitled to the same economic interests to which former holders of shares of Class B Common Stock were entitled before the Conversion, including with regard to dividends, liquidation rights and treatment in connection with a change of control or merger transaction, the Conversion had no impact on the economic interests of former holders of shares of Class B Common Stock.
•Capitalization. The Conversion had no impact on the total number of the Company’s outstanding shares of capital stock, as the shares of Class B Common Stock converted into an equivalent number of shares of Class A Common Stock. Pursuant to Section 243(b) of the DGCL, the filing of the Certificate of Retirement had the effect of amending the Certificate of Incorporation such that, upon the effectiveness of the Certificate of Retirement, the Company’s total number of authorized shares of capital stock was reduced by 7,825,000, representing the shares of Class B Common Stock retired in connection with the Conversion.
Item 5.03 - Amendments to Articles of Incorporation or Bylaws; Change in Fiscal Year.
As described under Item 3.03, on November 16, 2026, the Company filed the Certificate of Retirement with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware to effect the retirement of the shares of Class B Common Stock that were issued but not outstanding following the Conversion and to eliminate from the Certificate of Incorporation all references to the Class B Common Stock, pursuant to Section 243(b) of the DGCL. The Company subsequently filed 
a Restated Certificate of Incorporation with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on November 17, 2026, incorporating the amendments effected by the Certificate of Retirement (the “Restated Certificate”). 
The above descriptions of the Certificate of Retirement and the Restated Certificate do not purport to be complete and are qualified in their entirety by reference to the full text of the Certificate of Retirement and Restated Certificate, as applicable, which are attached as Exhibit 3.1 and Exhibit 3.2, respectively, and incorporated herein by reference.
Item 8.01 - Other Events.
The Class A Common Stock will continue to trade on The Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol “RIVN” following the Conversion and will maintain the same CUSIP number previously assigned to the Class A Common Stock.

NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2027
•Revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago
•Data Center revenue of $107.6 billion, up 110% from a year ago
•Vera Rubin NVL72, the most versatile and advanced computing platform ever built, has shipped
SANTA CLARA, Calif.—Nov. 17, 2026―NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today reported revenue for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, of $115.8 billion, up 20% from the previous quarter and up 103% from a year ago. For the quarter, GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were 74.8% and 74.9%, respectively. GAAP and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share were $2.70 and $2.68, respectively. 
“Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” said Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of NVIDIA. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.”
In September 2026, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors approved an increase of $150 billion to the company’s share repurchase authorization, without expiration. During the third quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA returned $28.1 billion to shareholders in the form of shares repurchased and cash dividends. As of the end of the third quarter, the company had approximately $227.3 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization. 
NVIDIA will pay its next quarterly cash dividend of $0.25 per share on December 23, 2026, to all shareholders of record on December 2, 2026.

Outlook
NVIDIA’s outlook for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, which includes an additional week, is as follows:
•Revenue is expected to be $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%. NVIDIA is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in its outlook.
•GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be between 71.0% and 72.0%. 
•GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be approximately $11.0 billion and $10.7 billion, respectively. 
•For the full year fiscal 2027, NVIDIA expects GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates to be between 16.0% and 18.0%, excluding any discrete items and material changes to NVIDIA’s tax environment.
Highlights
Data Center 
•Third-quarter revenue was $107.6 billion, up 21% from the previous quarter and up 110% from a year ago. 
•Ramped production and began shipping NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 — the fastest product ramp in the company’s history — with racks running at partners including CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and Nebius, and coming online soon at SpaceXSI.
•Expanded the Vera Rubin cloud ecosystem, announcing general availability of Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and Vera CPUs on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, general availability of Google Cloud’s Vera Rubin-powered A5X instances and the continued buildout of SpaceXSI’s infrastructure. 
•Announced Vera Rubin open architecture advances to help the industry scale faster, and revealed that Cisco, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Visionbay are joining many technology leaders advancing infrastructure for Vera Rubin. 
•Revealed that leading AI natives, cloud providers and neoclouds, including CoreWeave, Meta, Nebius, Nscale, OpenAI and Verda, are building with NVIDIA Vera CPUs to support the growing computing needs of businesses and developers, joining AWS, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and SpaceXSI.
•Expanded Anthropic’s access to NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin capacity through cloud providers, and continued to collaborate on design and engineering to optimize future NVIDIA architectures for Anthropic’s workloads.
•Announced the NVIDIA Vera CPU rack-scale platform for high-performance computing — combining NVIDIA’s first fully custom data center CPU with the gold standard for HPC networking to drive extreme efficiency and throughput for scientific modeling, simulation and agentic science.
•Introduced NVIDIA Rubin HPC, a new GPU in the Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. 
•Expanded collaboration with Meta on AI agent Muse and its family of models, with Meta planning expanded deployment of Vera Rubin, Vera CPUs, NVIDIA Spectrum-X™ networking and BlueField®-4 to scale training, inference and agents.
•Introduced DSX POD, a reference design for complete Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery to accelerate infrastructure deployment.
•Announced European ecosystem adoption of NVIDIA DSX™ to reduce AI factory power requirements and enable near-zero facility cooling water consumption.
•Announced that NVIDIA swept every MLPerf Training and Endpoints benchmark, and Vera Rubin NVL72 demonstrated leading inference performance in its MLPerf Inference preview debut.
•Launched NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform and introduced the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, combining open source OpenShell software, Vera Rubin for model inference, Vera CPUs

SAN
DIEGO, CALIFORNIA, November 12, 2026....Realty Income Corporation (Realty Income, NYSE: O), The Monthly Dividend Company®,
today announced that its Executive Vice President and Chief Strategy Officer, and President of Realty Income International, Neil Abraham,
will be leaving the company. To ensure a smooth transition, Mr. Abraham will continue to serve in his current role through December 31,
2026, and Realty Income intends to enter into a consulting agreement with Mr. Abraham through March 31, 2027.
“Neil
has been a valued member of the senior management team and a leader for the company,” said Sumit Roy, Realty Income’s President
and Chief Executive Officer. “On behalf of myself, the Board of Directors and the entire team at Realty Income, we want to thank
Neil for his partnership and contributions to many defining moments for the company over the past 11 years, and we wish him continued
success in his future endeavors.”
“Being
part of Realty Income’s growth has been one of the great joys of my career,” said Neil Abraham. “As I step into a new chapter
and explore fresh opportunities, I leave feeling proud of everything we built together. I’m grateful to my colleagues, the Board and
our partners for their support and trust along the way, and excited to watch Realty Income reach new heights in the years to come.”
About
Realty Income
Realty
Income (NYSE: O), an S&P 500 company, is real estate partner to the world’s leading companies®. Founded in
1969, we serve our clients as a full-service real estate capital provider. As of September 30, 2026, we have a portfolio of over 15,500
properties in all 50 U.S. states, the U.K., and eight other countries in Europe. We are known as “The Monthly Dividend Company®”
and have a mission to invest in people and places to deliver dependable monthly dividends that increase over time. Since our founding,
we have declared 677 consecutive monthly dividends and are a member of the S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats® index for
having increased our dividend for over 32 consecutive years. Additional information about the company can be found at www.realtyincome.com.

Item 5.02 Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers.
On November 13, 2026, Lowe’s Companies, Inc. (the “Company” or “Lowe’s”) appointed Margrethe (Margi) Vagell as Executive Vice President, Merchandising, effective November 14, 2026, succeeding William P. Boltz as part of his planned retirement. Ms. Vagell will also retain her responsibilities for Supply Chain, including the Company’s logistics, distribution centers, transportation and delivery services, and inventory replenishment and planning. Mr. Boltz will work closely with Ms. Vagell in the coming months to support a seamless transition. Following this transition, Mr. Boltz will serve as President of the Lowe’s Foundation (the “Foundation”), effective January 30, 2027. His appointment reinforces his long-standing commitment to the Foundation and its mission to build the skilled trades workforce. These leadership changes are designed to further connect the capabilities the Company has built through its Total Home Strategy and accelerate execution across the business.

Item 5.02. Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers.
 | | | | | | 
 | 
(i) | 
2027 Annual Bonus Plan
On November 17, 2026, upon the recommendation of the Executive Compensation and Human Resources Committee (the “Compensation Committee”), the Board of Directors (the “Board”) of Boston Scientific Corporation (the “Company”) approved the Company’s 2027 Annual Bonus Plan effective for the performance year of January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2027 (the “2027 Annual Bonus Plan”).
As part of the Company’s overall compensation program, the 2027 Annual Bonus Plan provides an annual cash incentive opportunity for eligible exempt and nonexempt indirect labor or equivalent personnel (including the Company’s named executive officers meeting the eligibility criteria) based on the achievement of certain performance metrics. The 2027 Annual Bonus Plan is substantially similar to the 2026 annual bonus plan and provides:
•for the performance year, an aggregate bonus pool equal to the total target annual bonuses of all plan participants multiplied by the applicable distribution percentage, as well a dynamic bonus pool, which shall be equal to 10% or less of the total target annual bonuses for all plan participants; 
•following the end of the performance year, the Compensation Committee shall determine the applicable distribution percentage (between 0% - 150%), based on the Company’s performance measured against Company-wide goals for global sales and adjusted earnings per share; provided the Board maintains its discretion to terminate, suspend or modify the 2027 Annual Bonus Plan and to reduce the applicable distribution percentage based on the Company’s performance relative to its quality objectives and performance of its quality systems; and
•managers will then assign each plan participant under their management an individual performance modifier (between 0% - 150%) based on such participant’s performance, which will be used to determine the participant’s final bonus award, resulting in a maximum payout potential for any individual participant of 0% - 225% of an individual’s target bonus, consistent with prior annual bonus plan years.
Awards to certain executive officers under the 2027 Annual Bonus Plan are subject to (i) the Company’s discretionary recoupment policy, which provides that, to the extent permitted by law, the Company may seek reimbursement of a bonus award in the event of an executive officer’s misconduct or gross dereliction of duty that results in a material violation of Company policy and causes significant harm to the Company and (ii) the Company’s Dodd-Frank Clawback Policy and any other compensation recovery policy adopted by the Board including in response to the requirements of Section 10D of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”), the final rules of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) thereunder, and any applicable listing rules or other rules and regulations implementing the foregoing or as otherwise required by law. 
This description of the 2027 Annual Bonus Plan does not purport to be complete and is subject to and qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of such plan. A copy of the 2027 Annual Bonus Plan is included in this filing as Exhibit 10.1 and incorporated herein by reference.
 | | | | | | 
 | 
(ii) | 
2027 Performance Share Programs
On November 17, 2026, upon the recommendation of the Compensation Committee, the Board approved the adoption of two performance share programs, the Boston Scientific Corporation 2027 Relative Total Shareholder Return Performance Share Program (the “2027 rTSR PSP”) and the Boston Scientific Corporation 2027 Organic Net Sales Growth Performance Share Program (the “2027 Organic Net Sales PSP”). The 2027 rTSR PSP and the 2027 Organic Net Sales PSP are substantially similar to the 2026 Total Shareholder Return Performance Share Program and the 2026 Organic Net Sales Growth Performance Share Program, respectively. These programs represent an important component of the overall mix of the Company’s long-term incentive program. Under both programs, if the relevant program criteria are met, performance share awards will be granted to the Company’s executive officers in the form of restricted stock units issued under the Company’s Amended and Restated 2011 Long-Term Incentive Plan. Awards to certain executive officers under both programs are subject to (i) the Company’s discretionary recoupment policy, which provides that, to the extent permitted by law, the Company may seek recovery of performance share units in the event of an executive officer’s misconduct or gross dereliction of duty that results in a material violation of Company policy and causes significant harm to the Company, and (ii) the Company’s Dodd-Frank Clawback Policy and any other compensation recovery policy adopted by the Board including in response to the requirements of Section 10D of the Exchange Act, the final rules of the SEC thereunder, and any applicable listing rules or other rules and regulations implementing the foregoing or as otherwise required by law.
 | | | | | | 
 | 
(A) | 
2027 Relative Total Shareholder Return Performance Share Program
The purpose of the 2027 rTSR PSP is to align the Company’s executive compensation program with the interests of stockholders and to reinforce the concept of pay for performance by comparing the Total Shareholder Return (“TSR”) of the Company’s common stock to the TSR of the other companies included in the S&P 500 Healthcare Index over a three-year period beginning on January 1, 2027 and ending on December 31, 2029 (the “Performance Period”). The number of performance shares awarded will be in a range of 0% to 200% of each participant’s target number of awards based on the Company’s TSR rank. Performance share awards will vest only upon satisfaction of both the performance criteria and the payment eligibility criteria set forth in the 2027 rTSR PSP, subject to certain exceptions in the event of a change of control or termination for retirement, death or disability. In the event a participant’s employment with the Company terminates due to retirement, as defined therein, prior to January 1, 2028, the performance share awards will be forfeited in their entirety.
This description of the 2027 rTSR PSP does not purport to be complete and is subject to and qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of such program. A copy of the 2027 rTSR PSP is included in this filing as Exhibit 10.2 and incorporated herein by reference.
 (B) 2027 Organic Net Sales Growth Performance Share Program
The purpose of the 2027 Organic Net Sales PSP is to align the Company’s executive compensation program with the interests of stockholders and to reinforce the concept of pay for performance by providing incentives for the achievement of key business performance objectives critical to the Company’s success. Under the 2027 Organic Net Sales PSP, performance will be measured by comparing the Company’s organic net sales growth, for the three-year period beginning on January 1, 2027 and ending on December 31, 2029 against its financial plan performance for organic net sales, as defined by the 2027 Organic Net Sales PSP. Organic net sales growth, as defined under the 2027 Organic Net Sales PSP, is net sales excluding the impact of foreign currency fluctuation and the impact of certain acquisitions and divestitures for which there are less than a full period of comparable net sales. The number of performance shares awarded will be in a range of 0% to 200% of each participant’s target number of awards, depending on such performance. Performance share awards will only vest upon satisfaction of both the performance criteria and the payment eligibility criteria set forth in the 2027 Organic Net Sales PSP, subject to certain exceptions in the event of a change of control or termination for retirement, death or disability. Item 1.01. Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement. 
On November 17, 2026 (the “Issue Date”), Cheniere Energy, Inc. (“Cheniere”) closed the sale of its previously announced offering of $1.2 billion aggregate principal amount of 5.800% Senior Notes due 2037 (the “Notes”). The Notes were issued at 99.313% of par. The sale of the Notes was not registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), and the Notes were sold in reliance on Rule 144A and Regulation S thereunder. 
Indenture 
The Notes were issued on the Issue Date pursuant to an indenture, dated as of March 19, 2026 (the “Base Indenture”), by and between Cheniere and The Bank of New York Mellon, as trustee (the “Trustee”), as supplemented by the third supplemental indenture, dated as of the Issue Date, between Cheniere and the Trustee, relating to the Notes (the “Third Supplemental Indenture”). The Base Indenture as supplemented by the Third Supplemental Indenture is referred to herein as the “Notes Indenture.” 
Under the terms of the Third Supplemental Indenture, the Notes will mature on March 15, 2037 and will accrue interest at a rate equal to 5.800% per annum on the principal amount from the Issue Date, with such interest payable semi-annually, in cash in arrears, on March 15 and September 15 of each year, beginning on March 15, 2027. 
The Notes are Cheniere’s senior unsubordinated obligations, ranking equally in right of payment with Cheniere’s other existing and future senior unsubordinated debt and senior in right of payment to any of Cheniere’s future subordinated debt. The Notes are not initially guaranteed by any of Cheniere’s subsidiaries. In the future, any subsidiary that guarantees or becomes a co-obligor with respect to any obligations of Cheniere in respect of Cheniere’s existing 4.625% senior notes due 2028 will also guarantee the Notes. 
At any time or from time to time prior to September 15, 2036 (the “Par Call Date”), Cheniere may, at its option, redeem all or part of the Notes at a redemption price equal to the greater of (i) 100% of the principal amount of the Notes to be redeemed and (ii) a specified make-whole redemption price set forth in the Third Supplemental Indenture, in either case plus accrued and unpaid interest to the redemption date. On and after the Par Call Date, Cheniere may redeem the Notes at its option, in whole at any time or in part from time to time at a redemption price equal to 100% of the principal amount of the Notes redeemed plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to (but not including) the applicable redemption date. 
The Notes Indenture also contains customary terms and events of default and certain covenants that, among other things, limit Cheniere’s ability to incur liens, enter into sale-leaseback transactions and consolidate, merge or sell, lease or otherwise dispose of all or substantially all of Cheniere’s properties or assets. The Notes Indenture covenants are subject to a number of important limitations and exceptions. 
The foregoing description of the Base Indenture is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Base Indenture, a copy of which is filed as Exhibit 4.1 to Cheniere’s Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) on March 19, 2026 and is incorporated by reference herein. The foregoing description of the Third Supplemental 
Indenture is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Third Supplemental Indenture, a copy of which is filed as Exhibit 4.2 hereto and is incorporated by reference herein. Any capitalized terms used herein and not otherwise defined have the meaning ascribed to them in the Notes Indenture. 
Registration Rights Agreement 
In connection with the issuance of the Notes, Cheniere and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, as representative of the initial purchasers, entered into a Registration Rights Agreement dated as of the Issue Date (the “Registration Rights Agreement”). Under the terms of the Registration Rights Agreement, Cheniere has agreed to use commercially reasonable efforts to file with the SEC and cause to become effective a registration statement with respect to an offer to exchange any or all of the Notes, for a like aggregate principal amount of debt securities of Cheniere issued under the Notes Indenture and identical in all material respects to the respective Notes sought to be exchanged (other than with respect to restrictions on transfer or to any increase in annual interest rate), and that are registered under the Securities Act. Cheniere has agreed to use commercially reasonable efforts to cause such registration statement to become effective within 360 days after the Issue Date. Under specified circumstances, Cheniere has also agreed to use commercially reasonable efforts to cause to become effective a shelf registration statement relating to resales of the Notes. Cheniere will be obligated to pay additional interest if it fails to comply with its obligations to register the Notes within the specified time periods. 
This description of the Registration Rights Agreement is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Registration Rights Agreement, a copy of which is filed as Exhibit 10.1 hereto and is incorporated by reference herein.

Pursuant to the Underwriting Agreement, the Company also granted the Underwriters an option to purchase up to an additional 5,000,000 Corporate Units to cover over-allotments. On November 17, 2026, the Company completed its offering of the 40,000,000 Corporate Units, including the exercise in full of the Underwriters’ over-allotment option.
Each Corporate Unit has a stated amount of $50 and is comprised of (i) a purchase contract (each, a “stock purchase contract”) which will obligate the holder to purchase from the Company, no later than December 15, 2029 (or, if such day is not a business day, on the following business day), a certain number of shares of the Company’s common stock, $0.01 par value (the “Common Stock”), for $50 in cash; (ii) a 1/40 undivided beneficial ownership interest in $1,000 principal amount of the Company’s Series 2026C Remarketable Senior Notes due 2031 (the “Series 2026C RSNs”); and (iii) a 1/40 undivided beneficial ownership interest in $1,000 principal amount of the Company’s Series 2026D Remarketable Senior Notes due 2034 (the “Series 2026D RSNs” and, together with the Series 2026C RSNs, the “RSNs”). Total annual distributions on the Corporate Units will be at the rate of 8.625% of the stated amount, consisting of quarterly contract adjustment payments under the stock purchase contracts in the amount of 3.125% per year and interest on the RSNs in the amount of 5.50% per year.
The RSNs were issued pursuant to the Senior Note Indenture, dated as of June 1, 2026 (the “Senior Note Indenture”), between the Company and U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association, as trustee, as supplemented, including by a Third Supplemental Indenture and a Fourth Supplemental Indenture, each dated as of November 17, 2026.
The stock purchase contracts were issued pursuant to a Purchase Contract and Pledge Agreement dated as of November 17, 2026 (the “Purchase Contract and Pledge Agreement”), between the Company and U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association, in its capacity as the purchase contract agent, collateral agent, custodial agent and securities intermediary.
Under the terms of the Purchase Contract and Pledge Agreement, the RSNs are pledged as collateral to secure the obligations of the holders of the Corporate Units to purchase the shares of Common Stock under the stock purchase contracts that form a part of the Corporate Units. Each of the RSNs will be remarketed, subject to certain terms and conditions, prior to the applicable stock purchase contract settlement date pursuant to the terms of the Purchase Contact and Pledge Agreement and a remarketing agreement to be entered into among the Company, U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association and a remarketing agent.
The Corporate Units were registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, pursuant to the shelf registration statement (Registration No. 333-296531) of the Company.
The foregoing disclosure is qualified in its entirety by reference to the Underwriting Agreement which is attached hereto as Exhibit 1.7, the Senior Note Indenture previously filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Third Supplemental Indenture, which is attached hereto as Exhibit 4.3(a), the Fourth Supplemental Indenture, which is attached hereto as Exhibit 4.3(b), the form of Series 2026C RSN, which is included in Exhibit 4.3(a) hereto, the form of Series 2026D RSN, which is included in Exhibit 4.3(b) hereto, the Purchase Contract and Pledge Agreement, which is attached hereto as Exhibit 4.12, and the forms of Remarketing Agreement, Corporate Unit and Treasury Unit, each of which is included in Exhibit 4.12 hereto.

items.text:
CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading | CFTC
/PressRoom/PressReleases/9327-26
 Skip to main content
Release Number 9327-26
CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
November 17, 2026
WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today released the agenda for an industry roundtable to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading.
The roundtable is taking place Dec. 15 from 1 to 4 p.m. EST at CFTC Headquarters, Three Lafayette Centre, 1155 21st St., NW, Washington, D.C. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9318-26].
Among other topics, attendees will discuss issues related to the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight and weekend trading, tokenization, margin, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness.
“From the outset of my chairmanship, I have been clear the CFTC will promote innovation in our derivatives markets in a manner attentive to the nuances of these markets and the varied asset classes that underpin them,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I look forward to hearing directly from industry stakeholders on the ways 24/7 trading would impact their respective business models to ensure the Commission is appropriately tailoring its regulatory regime for all market participants.”
View the full agenda here.
This meeting is open to the public and will be livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Dial-in information appears below. For the highest quality, select the number nearest your current location.
New York: 646-828-7666 
New Jersey: 551-285-1373 
San Jose: 669-254-5252 or 669-216-1590
US toll free: 833-568-8864 or 833-435-1820
US Spanish-language line: 646-964-1167 or 415-449-4000
International Numbers
Webinar ID: 165 708 9557
Passcode: 669856
Individuals with additional questions should contact [email protected].
The views, opinions, and information expressed by roundtable participants are solely those of the respective participants and do not necessarily reflect the views of the Commission, its staff, or the U.S. government.
-CFTC-

The Manufacturing and Trade Inventories and Sales estimates are based on data from three surveys: the Monthly Retail Trade Survey, the Monthly Wholesale Trade Survey, and the Manufacturers’ Shipments, Inventories, and Orders Survey. The purpose of this report is to provide broad and timely measures of combined changes in domestic retail trade, wholesale trade and manufacturers' activities.  1 https://ford.to/facebook https://x.com/ford https://ford.to/linkedin Ford Vice Chair John Lawler to Retire After more than three decades with Ford, Lawler leaves a legacy of global leadership and contributions across finance, operations, strategy and partnerships DEARBORN, MI — Nov. 17, 2026 — Ford Motor Company today announced that John Lawler, vice chair, will retire effective January 1, 2027, concluding a Ford career spanning more than three decades. Lawler’s Ford experience crossed the company’s global business, including finance roles in Japan, Europe and Asia Pacific; leadership in China; and senior responsibilities in strategy, autonomous vehicles and mobility partnerships. He became chief financial officer in 2020 and vice chair in 2024. In his vice chair role, he focused on strategy, partnerships, alliances and corporate development. “John has been an exceptional leader and a trusted partner to me and to Ford,” said Bill Ford, executive chair. “Over more than three decades, he has served this company with intelligence, integrity and a deep belief in Ford and its people. His leadership across our business and his contributions to Ford’s future have made a lasting difference. I’m grateful for all he has given Ford and wish him and his family every happiness in retirement.” “John has brought a rare combination of global experience, financial rigor and genuine care for Ford to every role he’s held,” said Jim Farley, president and CEO. “He helped lead our business through important periods of change, built strong teams and partnerships, and consistently challenged us to make thoughtful choices for the long term. I’ve valued his counsel and friendship, and I’m deeply grateful for his many contributions to Ford.” Ford has been preparing for John’s retirement and is focused on ensuring continuity across his areas of responsibility. John will remain in his role through the end of the year and, beginning January 1, 2027, his current responsibilities will be transitioned to: • Awenate Cobbina, CEO, Michigan Central, will report to executive chair Bill Ford; • Jim Baumbick, president, Ford Europe, will report to president and CEO Jim Farley; • Dave Carroll, president, Ford Energy, will report to president and CEO Jim Farley This planned transition is designed to be seamless for the company, its employees and its key stakeholders. Ford will not replace the vice chair role. “I’ve spent my entire career at Ford, and I’ve seen our industry—and our company—change in extraordinary ways,” said Lawler. “Through every chapter, what has mattered most is the people: the colleagues, employees and partners who took on challenges, adapted and moved Ford forward. I’m grateful to have been part of that journey, and confident that Ford is well positioned and has a bright future with the people who will shape what comes next.” 
 2 About Ford Motor Company Ford Motor Company (NYSE: F) is a global company based in Dearborn, Michigan, committed to helping build a better world, where every person is free to move and pursue their dreams. The company’s Ford+ plan for growth and value creation combines existing strengths, new capabilities, and always-on relationships with customers to enrich experiences for customers and deepen their loyalty. Ford develops and delivers innovative, must-have Ford trucks, sport utility vehicles, commercial vans and cars and Lincoln luxury vehicles, along with connected services, including BlueCruise (ADAS) and security. The company offers freedom of choice through three customer- centered business segments: Ford Blue, engineering iconic gas-powered and hybrid vehicles; Ford Model e, inventing breakthrough electric vehicles (“EVs”) along with embedded software that defines always-on digital experiences for all customers; and Ford Pro, helping commercial customers transform and expand their businesses with vehicles and services tailored to their needs. Additionally, the company provides financial services through Ford Motor Credit Company. Ford employs about 170,000 people worldwide. More information about the company and its products and services is available at corporate.ford.com.

Considerations at the Intersection of Payments and Tokenized Markets 
 Governor Christopher J. Waller 
At “Navigating the Future of Banking and Payments,” The Clearing House Annual Conference 2026, New York, New York 
 Share 
 Watch Live 
Thank you for inviting me to return and speak today.1 I am delighted to be here during a transformational time in payments. Two years ago, I spoke at The Clearing House's annual conference, where I discussed the roles that the private sector and the Federal Reserve play in payments.2 I argued that the public and private sectors have distinct but complementary roles. In particular, I emphasized that the private sector, through competition, is best positioned to develop solutions that benefit businesses and consumers and to fulfill a clear market need. 
The Federal Reserve can support these solutions by providing core payment and settlement infrastructure upon which the private sector can innovate, assessing potential risks to financial stability, and regularly engaging with the industry to better understand market challenges. Related to this last role, it's important to note that my remarks today are informed by rich, ongoing discussions I conduct with industry participants across a variety of forums, including a recent payments innovation roundtable I hosted at the Federal Reserve with participants from across traditional and decentralized finance, or DeFi.3 
Turning to the timely themes of the conference, many of the sessions focused on the evolving payments landscape, including the state of competition, technological advancements, and readiness for the future. With this backdrop in mind, today I will discuss some considerations for tokenization in the payment system with an eye toward the future and, in particular, the intersection of this technological advancement with existing systems and markets. To be clear, in this context, my focus is on the concept that a financial instrument can be represented digitally in "token" form and transacted on a new platform or technology, such as a distributed ledger technology like blockchain.4 
Although the terms "blockchain," "tokenization," and "smart contract" are widely used, to ensure we are on the same page, I want to give a simple explanation of each of these concepts. A blockchain is simply a database that can have a variety of management properties, such as who can hold a copy of the database, who can read the database, who can change the database, and how the database can be updated. The word block means data are added to the existing database in "blocks"—much like adding a new sheet of data to an existing Excel file.5 
Tokenization refers to the process of altering the properties of one form of an asset so that it can be transferred and used on a different platform than its current one. For example, if you go to a casino, you cannot use physical currency at the tables or machines. But you can take your cash and buy poker chips to use on the tables. In this world, poker chips are a tokenized version of physical cash that can be used instead of cash. 
Finally, a smart contract is simply a piece of code that is embedded in the database and can be triggered to execute an action at a given point of time or under a particular set of conditions. The key aspect of a smart contract is that all conditions of the code must be met simultaneously for the action to occur and be recorded on the blockchain. Smart contracts allow financial trades to be programmable, which is appealing for automating trades. 
In any financial trades on a blockchain, there is an object being bought (say, a tokenized share of stock) and there is a tokenized payment instrument being used to settle the trade. For example, stablecoins are starting to be used behind the scenes to settle obligations among participants in card networks. And The Clearing House is one of several groups building a network for clearing and settling tokenized deposits, which are digital transformations of the digits in your checking account that can then be used as a payment instrument to execute a blockchain trade. 
Now, let's look a bit closer at how payment innovation has progressed since I was here last. After a sustained period of industry investment and activity, a convergence between blockchain technologies and established markets is clearly under way, and deepening connections between these systems are taking root. Just a few years ago, blockchains were primarily used for crypto-asset trading activities. Today, all kinds of assets—from stocks to bonds to commodities—are being tokenized for use on blockchain networks to take advantage of new capabilities like programmability. And established payment providers, financial institutions, and market infrastructures are leveraging these capabilities. Firms are using these technologies to improve existing services—both customer facing and back office—and introduce new ones. 
At any point of convergence, such as those I have described, key questions arise that must be addressed before progress can continue. Let me focus on three areas. First, I will share observations on how tokenization is increasing competition between new and existing players, leading to a variety of solutions and choices for market participants to sort through. Second, I will discuss the importance of building trust in new tokenized services if they are to scale. Third, I will turn to how payments can support safe and efficient tokenized markets, where the same themes of competition, choice, and trust apply. Along the way, I will highlight open questions market participants should consider. I will close with some thoughts on ways the Federal Reserve can continue to support innovation in payments. 
Observations and Key Questions
Competition Dynamics
Tokenization is changing the nature of competition in payments. I am a firm believer in the free market and consider it the best testing ground for new, more efficient ways to deliver products and services, including through the introduction of new technologies.6 Blockchains in particular have some distinguishing features that make them ripe ground for competition in payments and financial markets. By operating 24/7/365, open blockchain networks offer a new paradigm for competition with traditional payment rails. In addition, smart contract code is often open source, or available to the general public. You or I could code and launch a smart contract today. 
When a technology such as blockchain is introduced, it can often set off a race between new entrants and established firms. Each has relative advantages. The new entrants bring native familiarity with the new technology and its potential to improve efficiency or enable new ways of doing business. But established firms, too, have distinct advantages: They have amassed customer relationships and associated network effects, along with the power of market confidence. History is replete with examples of success from both ends of the field. 
This competitive dynamic currently applies to the closely linked domains of payments and financial markets and could lead to more choices for consumers and businesses. Take, for example, DeFi firms, which first emerged to offer complex forms of lending and trading activity using crypto-assets, such as bitcoin and Ethereum. This activity was largely separated from regulated financial markets. As time has passed, there has been a better understanding of the potential for crypto technologies to improve existing payment systems and financial markets. 
These new technologies are forcing established firms to compete in a number of ways. In some cases, firms are developing their own blockchains where they maintain final control over the ledger. In other cases, firms are pooling their resources to develop tokenized products and services or blockchains owned by a consortium. In still other cases, experienced institutions are developing new tokenized products and services in partnership with emerging blockchain firms. 
Tokenization is still in the early innings of robust competition among new entrants, established firms, and combinations of each. Each model has its own benefits and tradeoffs among control and scale, and time will tell how these play out. Is it necessary for the market to coalesce around one model? I find it more likely that several different solutions will emerge to support different customers and use cases. But a market with many new options raises a further question: Which of them can be trusted? 
The Trust Imperative
I now want to turn to what I'll call the trust imperative that is affecting the development of tokenization. For new tokenized services to succeed, they will need more than just technical prowess. They will also need to earn trust through how reliably they operate and how clearly they are governed. It is therefore encouraging to hear that the conversation about which aspects of tokenization need to scale is increasingly focused on trust and governance. Trust is built when transactions occur reliably and securely, both within and across platforms. It is hard to win and easy to lose. In payments, trust is measured not in months and quarters, but in years and even decades. From a public policy perspective, I am acutely aware of the importance of trust in payments. 
As traditional financial assets move onto blockchains, tokenized services raise new questions about accountability. Who bears responsibility when fraudsters take advantage of the automatic execution of smart contracts? How will operators of new systems take responsibility for compromised or lost keys, erroneous transfers, and pricing errors? What happens to assets that are stranded on failed blockchains—the inevitable "zombie chains"?7 The recent events around Binance have highlighted some of the issues that can arise from programmable blockchains.8 
Answering these questions around trust is not merely a matter of finding the right solutions to purely technical problems. Industry debates are evolving to recognize that clear governance, sound legal frameworks, and common data and standards are just as important, if not more. Assets that move across networks must maintain legal identity, ownership rights, economic terms, compliance obligations, corporate-action treatment, and access to liquidity. Clear legal treatment of tokenized claims, settlement records, custody, insolvency, and resolution will be critical to mainstream institutional adoption—especially when assets are used in the most technically complex, smart contract–enabled arrangements. 
Ultimately, the market will determine which solutions deserve broader business and consumer trust. These solutions must strike the right balance between controls and the creative potential of blockchains. As I mentioned earlier, this balance may be use-case sp

NIKE, Inc. Announces Full Stride Ahead Strategy and 2031 Financial Framework at Investor Day
•Introduces Full Stride Ahead, NIKE's strategy to get closer to athletes* and deliver sustainable, profitable growth
•Reaffirms fiscal 2027 financial guidance
•Establishes 2031 financial framework targeting approximately $5 billion in incremental revenue growth, with fiscal 2027 as the base, and operating margins** of 12-14% and adjusted EPS(1) of $3.00 to $3.50 by the end of fiscal 2031
•Expects approximately $12 billion of cumulative capital returns through dividends to shareholders from fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2031
•Unveils next generation of innovation across Performance Sports and Sportswear
BEAVERTON, Ore., November 17, 2026 — NIKE, Inc. (NYSE: NKE) today will host its 2026 Investor Day at the Philip H. Knight Campus in Beaverton, Oregon, at 8:30 a.m. PT. The Company will introduce Full Stride Ahead, its strategy to get closer to athletes and focus resources on the greatest opportunities for long-term growth. NIKE will also outline its 2031 financial framework.
"NIKE is at its best when we start with the athlete and bring the full power of the Company together around sport," said Elliott Hill, President and Chief Executive Officer of NIKE, Inc. "Sport has never played a bigger role in people's lives, and as the leader in a growing $330 billion athletic footwear and apparel industry, the opportunity ahead of us has never been greater. Over the last two years, our Win Now actions have strengthened our foundation. Full Stride Ahead builds on that progress — bringing greater focus, speed and discipline to how we serve athletes and compete around the world."
Mr. Hill continued, "We're concentrating our resources where we have the greatest potential to win. We're also changing how we operate — delivering breakthrough products, building deeper local connections and moving faster to capture demand. Together, these actions are designed to return NIKE to sustainable, profitable growth."
Full Stride Ahead: Getting Closer to Athletes and Driving Sustainable, Profitable Growth
NIKE, Inc. has a portfolio of three distinct brands — Nike, Jordan and Converse. Each has a unique role to play, amplified by the shared capabilities and global scale of NIKE, Inc.
Within this portfolio, NIKE, Inc. will focus on the Performance Sports and Sportswear opportunities with the greatest potential for long-term growth. This includes five priority Performance Sports — Running, Training, Global Football, Basketball and Outdoor — and Sportswear, which encompasses Nike Sportswear, Jordan and Converse. Together with resources focused on 23 priority countries, these dimensions are expected to drive more than 90% of NIKE, Inc.'s revenue growth through fiscal 2031.
To capture these growth opportunities and create long-term shareholder value, NIKE, Inc. is advancing three connected strategic pillars: 
EPIC – Create Athlete Demand 
EPIC is designed to create demand through breakthrough innovation, distinctive products and compelling storytelling and experiences that inspire athletes. 
The Company will:
•Accelerate the Sport Offense across priority Performance Sports
•Scale breakthrough innovations into platforms that reach more athletes across more sports
•Bring greater newness, distinction and cultural relevance to Nike Sportswear
•Restore Jordan's premium positioning and marketplace health
•Sharpen Converse's lifestyle focus and strengthen its connection to creative culture
CONNECTED – Deepen Local Relevance
CONNECTED is designed to deepen relationships with local athletes and communities, translating insights into more relevant products, stories and experiences, online and in stores. 
The Company will:
•Move authority and resources closer to priority countries and cities
•Build deeper relationships with athletes and communities on the ground
•Bring our brands to life through locally relevant storytelling and experiences
•Work with our marketplace partners to tailor product assortments and experiences to local athletes
•Continue the reset in Greater China and accelerate growth across other priority markets
FAST – Capture Demand Faster and Operate More Efficiently 
FAST is designed to capture more of the demand it creates by responding faster and operating more efficiently. 
The Company will:
•Connect demand, inventory, supply and financial decisions through integrated planning 
•Build a more flexible and responsive supply network
•Simplify and standardize processes to improve execution and productivity
•Accelerate product creation to bring new innovations to athletes faster
•Use data, technology and AI to improve decision-making, speed and efficiency
Fiscal 2027 Outlook
NIKE, Inc. is reaffirming its guidance for fiscal 2027. The Company continues to expect fiscal 2027 revenue to decline in the high-single digit range and operating income** to decline faster than revenue, resulting in an adjusted operating margin(2) of approximately 6% and adjusted EPS of $1.15 to $1.35, which excludes approximately $0.15 per share of restructuring expenses related to Pace*** for fiscal 2027. The Company expects to return approximately $2.4 billion to shareholders through dividends in fiscal 2027.
2031 Financial Framework
NIKE's 2031 financial framework establishes a path to sustainable, profitable growth. Using fiscal 2027 as the base, by fiscal 2031, the Company is targeting approximately $5 billion in incremental revenue growth. Performance Sports are expected to be the primary engine of growth, contributing approximately $4 billion of the incremental $5 billion of revenue growth, with Sportswear contributing approximately $1 billion.
Fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 represent a period of investment toward growth, focused on strengthening the underlying quality of the business. Revenue declines are expected to moderate in fiscal 2028, with NIKE targeting a return to market-level revenue growth in fiscal 2029. In fiscal 2030 and fiscal 2031, the Company expects revenue growth to accelerate and exceed market growth as its strategic investments gain traction, revenue quality improves and previously announced productivity initiatives contribute more fully to financial performance.
Pace is expected to drive approximately $2.5 billion of annualized run-rate savings by fiscal 2031 with benefits beginning in fiscal 2027 and ramping up in fiscal 2029 and fiscal 2030. NIKE expects to incur approximately $1.3 billion in pre-tax charges associated with implementing Pace, which includes $0.3 billion recognized in fiscal 2026 and $0.3 billion expected in fiscal 2027 for severance-related costs.
Higher-quality revenue, gross margin expansion and productivity improvements are expected to drive operating margins of 12-14% by the end of fiscal 2031. Together, these drivers are expected to deliver adjusted EPS of $3.00 to $3.50 by the end of fiscal 2031.
Including fiscal 2027, the Company plans to return approximately $12 billion of cumulative capital to shareholders through dividends through the end of fiscal 2031, reinforcing its commitment to delivering shareholder returns while investing to restore sustainable growth.

MongoDB acquires Firebolt to bring lightning-fast real-time analytics into its Intelligent Data Platform Real-time analytics on live operational data, built so applications and AI agents can act on what’s happening now. Author: Fred Roma, SVP, Atlas Data Services The most valuable analytics no longer live in a dashboard. They live inside the application. A logistics app reroutes a shipment around a delay. A retail system reorders inventory before the shelf goes empty. A payments platform flags unusual behavior before the transaction clears. Each of these decisions requires comparing live operational data against historical patterns. Which routes are backing up, and is that normal? What’s selling faster than usual, and should we restock? Is this login typical for this account at this time of day? Enterprises that can answer these questions in the moment adapt as conditions change. Those that can’t are reacting to yesterday. Data infrastructure has long been split into two worlds: operational databases that run applications, and data warehouses that analyze what already happened. That paradigm was built for humans looking at morning dashboards, where data a few hours or days old was fine. As analytics moved into applications, real-time analytics emerged as a category of its own, combining complex queries over massive datasets with the speed, freshness, and concurrency that live applications demand. Agents raise the bar on all three. They act continuously, can drive thousands of concurrent queries, and need sub-second answers on fresh data. As businesses rely more on agents, real-time analytics becomes a core part of their data infrastructure. Eliminate the data-movement tax Running analytics on operational data often means copying it into a separate system, forcing organizations to build and maintain data pipelines, keep systems in sync, and run yet another platform. Even once the data is flowing, the added complexity, operational overhead, infrastructure cost, and risk of stale answers remain. This is the data-movement tax, and it compounds as agents drive more decisions. Systems that require customers to move and synchronize data across separate platforms often struggle to deliver fresh answers at the speed and scale that live applications need. For MongoDB customers, the operational data their applications and agents rely on is already in MongoDB, so analytics should be able to run there too, at the source. That's why MongoDB acquired Firebolt. One platform for operational data and real-time analytics By integrating Firebolt into MongoDB’s Intelligent Data Platform, we’re bringing a high-performance analytics engine to where your operational data already lives. Firebolt’s engine will run right alongside your database, and we’ll keep it in sync automatically, so there’s no pipeline to build or manage. You’ll 
get one platform for operational and real-time analytical workloads, so teams can ship faster, with fewer systems to operate and secure. Our Intelligent Data Platform already brings together operational data, search and vector search, Voyage AI models, stream processing, and the ability to build and run agents in production. Real-time analytics will extend that foundation, enabling applications and agents to analyze live data and act on it in the moment. Over time, customers will also be able to analyze data from other sources and formats alongside their MongoDB data. When analytics powers a live application, an outage no longer just delays a report. It breaks the customer experience or stalls an agent mid-decision. MongoDB operates in this mission-critical world: today, approximately 75% of the Fortune 100 trust MongoDB with applications that require the highest levels of security, durability, and availability. We’re bringing that same level of reliability and operational excellence to real-time analytics. Why Firebolt, and what’s next Firebolt’s analytics engine is proven in production. It was built from the start for the high concurrency required by live applications and agents, not just internal dashboards and reports. Similarweb, for example, uses Firebolt to power complex, customer-facing analytics over more than a trillion rows at petabyte scale, with dynamic queries delivering sub-second performance without extensive pre- aggregation. Firebolt’s team has tackled some of the hardest problems in analytical engines. CEO Benjamin Wagner’s background is in analytical database research at the Technical University of Munich. He built the Munich engineering team behind Firebolt’s engine and led engineering before becoming CEO. CTO Mosha Pasumansky was an architect of Microsoft Analysis Services, co-invented the MDX query language, and led the technical development of Dremel and BigQuery at Google. “Firebolt was designed for the cloud to do what many people believed was impossible: low-latency, high- QPS analytics with fast-changing data on object storage,” says Mosha Pasumansky, Firebolt’s CTO. “We also knew that today’s applications deal with complex and flexible schemas, the kind MongoDB’s document model supports natively. So we made sure to keep the benefits of columnar storage and vectorized processing on those schemas through smart automatic column shredding.” “Firebolt and MongoDB share the same DNA,” says Benjamin Wagner, Firebolt’s CEO. “We both build mission-critical data infrastructure for engineers. We spent the last several years building an analytics engine for what live applications and agents demand: high-concurrency, sub-second answers on fresh data. Joining MongoDB puts our engine where millions of developers already build. We can’t wait to bring real-time analytics to MongoDB customers.” We’re thrilled to welcome the Firebolt team to MongoDB, and our teams are already working together to bring Firebolt’s engine into MongoDB. In the coming months, customers will be able to turn on real-time analytics for their MongoDB data, so their applications and agents can act on what’s happening now. More to come soon. Join the waitlist to be among the first to try real-time analytics on MongoDB. ============== 
What is Firebolt? Firebolt is a high-performance analytical database designed for low-latency queries and high- concurrency applications. Do Firebolt and real-time analytics replace a data warehouse? No. Traditional data warehouses and data lakes remain the right fit for internal BI, reporting, and data science. Real-time analytics is for application-facing analytics, which has a different set of requirements: complex queries over massive datasets, sub-second responses, high concurrency, and fresh data for live applications and AI agents. What happens to existing Firebolt customers? Nothing changes for existing Firebolt customers. They can continue using the product with the same support and service. Firebolt’s customers are a big reason we wanted to bring this team and engine into MongoDB. They’ve shown what the technology can do under real production load. On November 17, 2026, JPMorgan Chase & Co. ("JPMorganChase" or the “Firm”) announced that Bregje de Best, 43, will succeed Jeremy Barnum as Chief Financial Officer (“CFO”) of the Firm, following its first-quarter 2027 financial reporting. At that time, Ms. de Best will join the Firm's Operating Committee, and Mr. Barnum will become a Vice Chairman of the Firm.
Ms. de Best currently serves as the CFO of the Commercial & Investment Bank (“CIB”), a position she has held since June 2025. Prior to her role as the CFO of CIB, Ms. de Best was the co-head of Global Corporate Banking from March 2024 to June 2025. Previously, Ms. de Best was co-head of Global Corporate Derivatives for the Firm’s Investment Bank from 2019 to 2024. Before that, she held other senior roles in investment banking and markets in the United Kingdom and Asia. Ms. de Best joined the Firm in 2006. 
A copy of the press release related to this announcement is attached hereto as Exhibit 99.1.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. 270 Park Avenue, NY 10017-2014 NYSE symbol: JPM www.jpmorganchase.com News release: IMMEDIATE JPMorganChase announces Bregje de Best will succeed Jeremy Barnum as Chief Financial Officer following first-quarter 2027 financial reporting. Barnum to become a Vice Chairman at that time. New York, November 17, 2026 – JPMorganChase announced today that Bregje de Best, Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of the Commercial & Investment Bank (CIB), will succeed Jeremy Barnum as CFO of the company following its first-quarter 2027 financial reporting. At that time, de Best will join the firmwide Operating Committee (OC), and Barnum will become a Vice Chairman of the company. Barnum informed the company of his intention to conclude his tenure as CFO after six years in the role and to support the transition to the next generation of talent. He and de Best will work closely between now and the change to ensure a smooth transition, with Barnum leading the January and April earnings announcements and the company’s Investor Day in February. Following first-quarter financial reporting, Barnum will become a Vice Chairman and has agreed to stay on until early 2028, helping Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Jamie Dimon and other senior leaders on a range of firmwide initiatives. “Jeremy has been an outstanding CFO of our company since 2021 and is enormously respected both internally by our leadership team and employees as well as outside the company by investors, analysts and others. After many years in the job, he asked to transition leadership of Finance to another outstanding executive. I’m excited he will be helping Bregje through this period and taking on a Vice Chairman role, where he can continue to be such a valuable advisor and partner to me and our OC,” said Jamie Dimon. Barnum said: “My years as CFO at JPMorgan Chase have been among the most challenging and fulfilling of my life, and I am very grateful to Jamie for the opportunity to serve the company and its shareholders as well as for his mentorship and support. I couldn’t be happier to have Bregje as my successor to continue the tradition of excellence in our Finance organization, and I am very grateful to my team for their support during my time as CFO. During my remaining time at the company, I’m looking forward to helping with the many challenges present in the current environment.” As CFO of the CIB, de Best oversees Finance, Business Management and Controls for our Global Banking, Markets, Payments and Securities Services businesses. Prior to that, she was co-head of Global Corporate Banking, which serves large corporates, financial institutions and public-sector organizations. Previously, she held other senior roles in investment banking and markets in the U.K. and Asia.

I’m very excited she will become our company’s next CFO.” Early next year, the company will announce a successor to de Best as CFO of the CIB. JPMorgan Chase & Co. 101 East Main Street

Humana Announces Pricing Terms of Offers to Purchase for Cash Certain of its Outstanding Debt Securities 
Louisville, KY - November 16, 2026 - Humana Inc. (NYSE: HUM) (“Humana”, “we”, or “our”) today announced the Reference Yield and Total Consideration (as set forth in the table below) to be paid in connection with its previously announced cash tender offers (collectively, the “Offers”) to purchase the outstanding notes described below, in each case upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Offer to Purchase dated November 9, 2026 (the “Offer to Purchase”). 
The Notes offered to be purchased in the Offers, in the order of acceptance priority, are the 2.150% Senior Notes due 2032; 3.125% Senior Notes due 2029; 3.700% Senior Notes due 2029; 4.875% Senior Notes due 2030; 1.350% Senior Notes due 2027; 3.950% Senior Notes due 2027; 5.375% Senior Notes due 2031; and 5.750% Senior Notes due 2028 (collectively, the “Notes” and each a “Series of Notes”) for the consideration described below, up to an aggregate purchase price, excluding the Accrued Coupon Payment (as defined below), of $1,500,000,000 (the “Tender Cap”) subject to proration and the application of the Acceptance Priority Levels set forth in the table below and as further set forth in the Offer to Purchase and the terms and conditions, including, among others, an $800,000,000 cap on the aggregate principal amount to be accepted for purchase of the 5.375% Senior Notes due 2031 (the “2031 Notes”) pursuant to the Offers (the “Series Cap”) and the Acceptance Priority Procedures set forth in the Offer to Purchase. The 2031 Notes may be subject to proration both due to the Acceptance Priority Procedures and the Series Cap such that Humana will only accept for purchase an aggregate principal amount of the 2031 Notes up to the Series Cap. Subject to applicable law, Humana may, but is under no obligation to, eliminate, increase or decrease the Tender Cap and/or the Series Cap. In the event proration is required with respect to a Series of Notes, Humana will multiply the principal amount of each valid tender of such Series of Notes by the applicable proration rate and round the resulting amount down to the nearest integral multiple of the Authorized Denomination, in order to determine the principal amount of such tender that will be accepted pursuant to the applicable Offer. The excess principal amount of Notes not accepted from the tendering Holders will be promptly returned to such Holders, and if this excess principal amount of Notes is less than $1,000, Humana may either accept or reject all such tendering Holders’ validly tendered Notes in its sole discretion. Additionally, Humana may increase the amount of Notes accepted for payment in any Offer by no more than 2% of the outstanding Notes of the applicable Series, as further described in the Acceptance Priority Procedures set forth in the Offer to Purchase, without amending or extending the Offer. The Offer to Purchase and any related documents are referred to herein collectively as the “Tender Offer Documents”. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this press release have the meanings given to them in the Offer to Purchase.

Item 5.02. Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers.
Election of Directors
(d) On November 16, 2026, the Board of Directors (the "Board") of S&P Global Inc. (the "Company"), on recommendation of its Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, appointed Kfir Godrich to serve as a member of the Board (a "Director") of the Company, effective January 1, 2027. Mr. Godrich was appointed to serve on the Board’s Audit Committee. As a Director, Mr. Godrich will participate in the Company’s standard non-employee Director compensation program effective January 1, 2027. Under the program, Mr. Godrich will receive an annual cash retainer of $110,000, an annual equity award with a grant date value of $245,000 and, for his service as a member of the Audit Committee, an additional annual cash retainer of $20,000. Mr. Godrich will also be eligible to participate in the Company’s Director Deferred Stock Ownership Plan, included as Appendix B to the Company's Definitive Proxy Statement on Schedule 14A ("Proxy Statement") that was filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") on March 19, 2024, and the Company’s Director Deferred Compensation Plan, included as an exhibit to the Company's Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2007 that was filed with the SEC on February 29, 2008. With the appointment of Mr. Godrich, the Board has acted to approve an increase in the size of the Board from ten to eleven Directors.
There is no arrangement or understanding between Mr. Godrich and any other persons pursuant to which Mr. Godrich was selected as a Director. There are no transactions between Mr. Godrich and the Company that are required to be reported under Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K.

S&P Global Adds Kfir Godrich to its Board of Directors
•Mr. Godrich brings extensive experience in enterprise technology, cybersecurity, data, and AI
•Appointment effective January 1, 2027; Mr. Godrich will serve on the Board's Audit Committee
NEW YORK (November 17, 2026) — S&P Global (NYSE: SPGI) today announced that its Board of Directors has approved the appointment of Kfir Godrich to the Board, effective January 1, 2027. 
Mr. Godrich most recently served as Chief Innovation Officer, and previously as Global Head of Technology, at BlackRock, Inc., where he led enterprise technology, cybersecurity, data, and AI with responsibility for a significant share of the firm's technology operations and served on its Global Operating Committee. He led the development of BlackRock's enterprise data platform and AI Labs, embedded AI across business workflows, and was instrumental in migrating the Aladdin platform to the cloud.
Earlier in his career, Mr. Godrich held senior roles at Hewlett-Packard focused on cloud, data center and enterprise technology strategy. Prior to that, he held leadership roles in mission-critical infrastructure, telecommunications, energy and data center technology at EYP Mission Critical Facilities and eNetPower.
"Kfir is an experienced and innovative technology and business leader who operates at the leading edge of AI, cybersecurity and quantum computing," said Martina L. Cheung, President and CEO, S&P Global. "As we see the convergence between financial and physical markets, he also brings unique strengths to the S&P Global Board with his background in digital infrastructure and energy."
"We are very pleased to welcome Kfir to the S&P Global Board," said Ian P. Livingston, Non-Executive Chairman of the Board, S&P Global. "His deep experience in enterprise technology, cybersecurity and large-scale transformation will strengthen the Board’s expertise and bring valuable perspective as we support Martina and her team in delivering long-term value for our customers and shareholders."
"It is an honor to join the Board of S&P Global," said Kfir Godrich. "Technology continues to create significant new opportunities for companies and their clients, and I look forward to bringing my experience and perspective to the Board as S&P Global continues to innovate and grow."
Mr. Godrich will serve on the Board's Audit Committee.

Item 7.01 Regulation FD disclosure
This document provides summary supplemental segment financial information for fiscal years 2024, 2025 and 2026 to reflect the following:
Shift of Disney Consumer Products Businesses to Entertainment
To more directly link our consumer products businesses with the creative and business teams behind the content, we will shift the following consumer products businesses from the Experiences segment to the Entertainment segment, and, effective with the first quarter of fiscal 2027, the financial results of these businesses will be reported as part of the Entertainment segment:
◦Merchandise Licensing, which includes the licensing of our trade names, characters, visual, literary and other intellectual property (IP) to various manufacturers, game developers, publishers and retailers throughout the world, for use on merchandise, published materials and games
◦Publishing, which includes the development and publishing of books, comic books and magazines primarily sold through wholesalers
Within the Experiences segment, the remaining consumer products business, Branded Retail, which consists of branded merchandise sold online and at retail locations, will be reported as part of Domestic Parks and Experiences.
Presentation of Entertainment Revenues
Effective with the first quarter of fiscal 2027, the Company will report Entertainment segment revenues as follows:
◦Subscription-video-on-demand (SVOD) services, primarily consisting of subscription fees and advertising
◦Content and IP, primarily consisting of content sales and consumer products
◦Linear networks and virtual multi-channel video programming distributor (vMVPD) services, primarily consisting of subscription and affiliate fees and advertising
Exclusion of Equity Income from Entertainment Segment Operating Results 
On September 30, 2026, we sold our 50% interest in A+E Global Media, which was the most significant equity investment included in the Entertainment segment. Effective with the first quarter of fiscal 2027, the Company will exclude equity income from Entertainment segment operating results.
The information contained in this Item 7.01, including Exhibit 99.1 incorporated herein by reference, is furnished and shall not be deemed to be filed for purposes of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, or otherwise subject to the liabilities of that section, nor shall such information be deemed incorporated by reference in any filing under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, except as shall be expressly set forth by specific reference in such filing.
